units.function: Unit tests fixing the default external feedback destination and verifying a full FeedbackTraceBundle is wrapped as gzip/base64 JSON with an optional bearer token before upload.
units.dependencyDirection: Feedback export URL/token configuration and a trace bundle enter a fetch-based client; compressed data leaves the server for the configured or Paperclip-operated telemetry endpoint.
units.keyDataModels: Trace/export/Company/Issue/adapter identifiers, capture status, envelope, run/raw/normalized traces, privacy/integrity/files, object key, gzip+base64 encoding and bearer token.
units.lifecycle: With no URL configured the client posts to telemetry.paperclip.ing; with a token it serializes objectKey/exportedAt/bundle, synchronously gzips and base64-encodes the payload, then sends it as JSON.
units.testAssessment: The payload decoding assertion precisely documents the transmitted envelope and destination. It does not cover consent/company sharing gates, prior redaction, HTTPS/private-address validation, token leakage, timeout/cancellation, payload limits, idempotency, retries after ambiguous success, redirects, response schema, non-2xx bodies or structured audit receipts.
units.designRationale: Make user-authorized diagnostic sharing work without self-hosters configuring a backend and reduce payload size through a simple transport-neutral envelope.
units.companyOsProblem: Enterprise data export must be disabled by default, destination-specific, policy-evaluated and provable even when a user asks to share diagnostics.
units.companyOsFit: Reject the implicit vendor endpoint and opaque whole-bundle upload contract. Company OS tests must require an enabled DataEgressPolicy, approved destination, manifest of fields/digests, accountable consent, redaction receipt, bounded asynchronous transfer, idempotency and a durable export receipt.
units.responsibilityConflict: The test proves transport shape but not that the exact exported fields were authorized. A default external destination can surprise self-hosted operators, and compression is not protection or evidence of consent.

units.function: Direct HTTP uploader for feedback trace bundles using a default Paperclip telemetry endpoint, optional plaintext configuration token and gzip/base64 request envelope.
units.dependencyDirection: Server config and shared FeedbackTraceBundle flow directly into global fetch; a remote JSON response supplies or overrides the returned object key.
units.keyDataModels: Backend base URL/token, date-partitioned Company object key, exportedAt, entire trace bundle, encoding marker, bearer header and remote objectKey/error text.
units.lifecycle: Client creation resolves a default endpoint; upload synchronously serializes/compresses the full bundle, posts it without an abort deadline, throws remote text or status on failure and accepts any nonempty response objectKey.
units.testAssessment: Implementation is small and deterministic but lacks protocol/host allowlisting, private-network/redirect defense, timeout/AbortSignal, size limits/streaming, idempotency key/content digest, retry classification, response validation, stable errors and SecretRef handling. A response-lost success can be retried under a different date-derived object key after midnight.
units.designRationale: Keep feedback export deployment-light and decouple server storage from the telemetry service's object layout.
units.companyOsProblem: The data-exit firewall must be the sole canonical owner of outbound enterprise payloads across managed and self-hosted profiles.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT behind DataEgressPort. Default is disabled/no destination; policy resolves a registered HTTPS sink and short-lived audience secret, blocks private/redirect escapes, streams a bounded immutable manifest, uses digest-bound idempotency, enforces timeout/retry/dead-letter policy and records consent plus delivery receipt.
units.responsibilityConflict: This client can transmit all bundle fields based only on caller behavior and ambient config; it has no Work/data contract, accountable approver, destination policy or field-level export proof. Remote error text may also enter local failure logs as untrusted content.

units.function: Deterministic recursive feedback sanitizer for current-user paths, credential-shaped structures/free text, PEM/JWT/provider keys, connection strings, email/phone PII, truncation metadata and SHA-256 digests.
units.dependencyDirection: Arbitrary feedback strings/JSON-like values enter shared structural redaction plus module-local regex patterns; sanitized values, transformation summary and deterministic hashes feed the feedback export bundle.
units.keyDataModels: Redacted/truncated/omitted field sets, notes/counts, regex kind/replacement, deterministic_feedback_v2 summary, canonicalized value and SHA-256 digest.
units.lifecycle: Text first removes current-user data then applies ordered secret/PII patterns and truncates; records pass through generic secret-field sanitization and recurse; summaries sort field/count metadata; stableStringify sorts object keys before hashing.
units.testAssessment: The design records what was transformed and applies defense-in-depth across structured and free text. In this unit there is no dedicated exhaustive test file; coverage is indirect through large feedback-service tests. Regex detection is necessarily incomplete, recursion/arrays are unbounded and cyclic values fail. Non-plain objects such as Buffer pass through, and the custom canonicalizer has undefined/sparse-array/non-finite-number collision or serialization-parity risks.
units.designRationale: Produce useful reproducible diagnostic traces while automatically removing common secrets, local identity and PII and exposing a machine-readable redaction summary.
units.companyOsProblem: Data egress needs deterministic minimization and a reviewable transformation receipt, but enterprise policy cannot rely on regex scrubbing after assembling an unrestricted bundle.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the transformation-summary and ordered deterministic pipeline. Company OS first constructs a typed allowlisted export manifest under DataAuthorization, rejects unknown/non-JSON shapes, enforces depth/count/byte limits, applies pluggable DLP rules and human preview, then hashes RFC-defined canonical bytes and retains source-to-export digest lineage.
units.responsibilityConflict: Heuristic redaction cannot establish authorization, completeness or non-disclosure. A digest over a custom ambiguous canonicalization is not adequate integrity evidence, and a redaction summary must identify policy/version/actor as well as transformations.
